newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. urges end to Afghan fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. urges end to Afghan fighting.

text.p: The United Nations on Thursday called on the warring factions in Afghanistan to stop fighting and start negotiations.

"UNSMA (U.N. Special Mission to Afghanistan) reiterates its urgent appeal to the parties concerned to settle their differences by means of negotiations and not by fighting," mission head Norbert Holl said in a statement.
"UNSMA has, with great concern, taken note of heavy fighting which has erupted in the past 48 hours in several areas in Afghanistan, particularly in Mazar-i-Sharif," Holl said.
The Taleban Islamic militia has been defeated by ethnic Uzbek forces in northern Mazar-i-Sharif after two-days of bloody fighting that left scores dead.
Uzbek troops led by General Abdul Malik are holding captive Taleban Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous and the Taleban northern military commander, Mullah Abdul Razzaq.
"(The UNSMA) deplores the loss of many lives and taking of prisoners, including those of political rank," Holl said.

"UNSMA offers it good offices to bring the warring parties together to discuss possibilities of overcoming the present critical situation and is prepared to facilitate contacts between both sidess," he said.

A Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday that the Taleban militia was holding peace talks with the opponents who drove it out of Mazar-i-Sharif. He said negotiations were "currently under way in Afghanistan".

Pakistan was the first country to recognise the Taleban government in Afghanistan after the purist Ismamic militia captured Mazar-i-Sharif, the main opposition stronghold in the north, on Saturday and has a consulate in the city.
